name: Peter
bio:
Simon, called Peter, was a fisherman on the Sea of Galilee when Jesus called him and his brother Andrew to follow him and become "fishers of men"; they immediately left their nets to do so (Matthew 4:18-20). John's Gospel records that Andrew, newly a disciple of Jesus, first brought his brother Simon to him; Jesus, on seeing him, renamed him Cephas, meaning "a stone" (John 1:40-42). His prominent, often impulsive role among the disciples is told in detail in the chapters ahead. Luke's account adds that this call came after Jesus taught from Peter's boat and then told him, despite a fruitless night of fishing, to let down his nets again; the catch was so great it nearly sank both boats, and Peter, astonished, fell at Jesus's knees crying, "Depart from me; for I am a sinful man, O Lord," before Jesus reassured him and he left everything to follow (Luke 5:1-11). When Jesus entered Peter's house, he healed Peter's mother-in-law of a fever with a touch (Matthew 8:14-15). When Jesus walked on the water during a storm, Peter asked to join him and briefly walked on the water himself, but began to sink when fear overtook his faith; Jesus caught him and gently rebuked his doubt (Matthew 14:28-31). When the disciples asked for clarification on Jesus's teaching that defilement comes from the heart rather than food, Peter was the one who asked him to explain the saying (Matthew 15:15-20).

 At Caesarea Philippi, when Jesus asked who the disciples believed he was, Peter declared him "the Christ, the Son of the living God"; Jesus blessed him for this Father-given revelation, declared he would build his church on this foundation, and gave him the keys of the kingdom of heaven. When Jesus then predicted his own coming death in Jerusalem, Peter rebuked him for it, and Jesus sharply called him "Satan" for thinking only in human terms (Matthew 16:13-23).

 Peter witnessed Jesus's transfiguration with Moses and Elijah, offering to build shelters for them before a voice from heaven interrupted. Later, when Capernaum's tax collectors questioned him about the temple tax, Jesus had him catch a fish with a coin in its mouth to pay it for them both (Matthew 17:1-27). Peter asked Jesus how many times he should forgive a repeatedly sinning brother, suggesting seven; Jesus answered "seventy times seven," teaching boundless forgiveness (Matthew 18:21-22). Peter asked Jesus what reward the disciples would receive for having given up everything to follow him; Jesus promised them thrones in the age to come, and that the last would be first (Matthew 19:27-30).

 Jesus sent Peter and John specifically to prepare the Passover meal for the Last Supper (Luke 22:8), and at the table warned him that Satan desired to sift him like wheat, but that he had prayed for his faith to endure, so that once restored he could strengthen the other disciples (Luke 22:31-32). At the Last Supper, Peter confidently insisted he would never desert Jesus even if everyone else did, but Jesus predicted he would deny him three times before dawn. At Gethsemane, Peter was among the three disciples Jesus took deeper into the garden, though he fell asleep each time Jesus checked on them. After Jesus's arrest, Peter followed at a distance into the high priest's courtyard, but when questioned three times about his association with Jesus, he denied knowing him each time, growing more emphatic with each denial; when the rooster crowed as predicted, Peter remembered Jesus's words and wept bitterly (Matthew 26:33-75). When Mary Magdalene, Joanna, and Mary the mother of James reported that Jesus's tomb was empty, Peter ran to see for himself, and found only the linen cloths left behind. Later that day, the risen Jesus appeared to Peter personally, as two disciples returning from Emmaus learned when they found the eleven already saying the Lord had appeared to Simon (Luke 24:1-12, 34). When Jesus's hard teaching about eating his flesh and drinking his blood caused many disciples to desert him and he asked the Twelve if they would also leave, Peter answered, "Lord, to whom shall we go? thou hast the words of eternal life," affirming his belief that Jesus was the Christ, the Son of the living God (John 6:66-69). At the Last Supper, when Jesus began washing the disciples' feet, Peter objected that Jesus should never wash his feet; told that otherwise he would have no part with Jesus, Peter asked to have his hands and head washed too, prompting Jesus to explain that one who is already clean need only have his feet washed (John 13:6-10). When Jesus said he was going where Peter could not yet follow, Peter asked why not, insisting he would lay down his life for him; Jesus replied that Peter would deny him three times before the rooster crowed (John 13:36-38).
